item.description:
Trump says Iran would be hit with 'no hesitation' if it threatens allies, US ships

US President Donald Trump said he could use military force against Iran with "no hesitation" if Washington's ships and allies are threatened.  

During an interview with the Salem News Channel, the US president was asked whether he would hesitate to use force to stop Iran from "terrorising our allies and our ships,".

"No hesitation. We’re doing very well with it right now," Trump answered. "But the answer is, if I saw things going the other way, I would do that, and it’s possible I would do it right now."

Trump claimed the US has suffered no losses in recent months, despite reports and official figures indicating that over a dozen soldiers have died as  a result of the war on Iran.

"We haven’t lost a soldier in five months, and we control the Gulf... Totally control it," he said.

Ghalibaf says 'ball is in America's court' for US-Iran peace talks
item.description:
Ghalibaf says 'ball is in America's court' for US-Iran peace talks

Iran's parliament speaker, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, said in an interview with Al Jazeera that Tehran has no desire to continue the war with the US, but that the ball is in Washington’s court for peace talks.

Ghalibaf said that Iran provided the US with a clear and transparent response outlining its demands, but the Trump administration has not yet responded.

An agreement with Washington is possible, he added, provided it adheres to what was previously agreed upon and refrains from actions that undermine trust and excessive demands.

He said that Iran is determined to move beyond the state of “no war, no peace” through negotiations or sustainable deterrence, and accused Washington of imposing a siege on the country by blocking access to food and hindering trade and healthcare services.

“As the saying goes, the ball is in America’s court.” Iran's parliament speaker, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, said in an interview with Al Jazeera that Tehran has no desire to continue the war with the US, but that the ball is in Washington’s court for peace talks. https://t.co/phdAbTbmQ8

item.title: Iran’s IRGC says it targeted US radar in Bahrain
item.description:
Iran’s IRGC says it targeted US radar in Bahrain

Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) announced that its forces targeted a US early-warning radar in Bahrain in retaliation to an attack on a telecommunications tower in Iran’s Sirik.

"This serves as a serious warning to the aggressor enemy to cease its aerial provocations and oil smuggling in the Strait of Hormuz. Should these violations and acts of aggression recur, the IRGC Aerospace Force stands in full readiness to engage without limits," the IRGC was quoted as saying by local media.

item.title: How Gaza’s winter ‘crisis’ is manufactured by Israel
item.description:
How Gaza’s winter ‘crisis’ is manufactured by Israel

For the fourth winter in a row, rains have swept through Gaza, exposing woefully inadequate supplies of materials for shelter entering the strip.

This has forced 65 percent of the population - around 1.4m people - to shelter in makeshift shelters or tents which have been swamped in the downpour, or damaged buildings which risk collapse.

While the weather is turbocharged by a strengthening El Nino event, the paucity of aid is entirely man-made, leveraged as a pressure point by Israel over Gaza’s population.

The Israeli authorities have long restricted the entry of shelter and construction materials into Gaza, with vital equipment like tent poles and mobile homes deemed to be “dual use”.

Read more: How Gaza’s winter ‘crisis’ is manufactured by Israel

item.title: Iran says 2 oil tankers caught fire after hitting naval mines near Strait of Hormuz
item.description: Two oil tankers caught fire Thursday after striking naval mines in restricted waters east of the Strait of Hormuz, Iran’s army said, according to Iranian broadcaster IRIB. In a statement, the army’s public relations department said the vessels entered a prohibited and unsafe area Thursday afternoon despite warnings and after switching off their radar systems. The army accused US President Donald Trump of bearing primary responsibility for the incident, also blaming the vessels’ owners for relying on what it described as misleading statements from Washington. item.title: Palestinian American says Israeli army bars him from entering his West Bank home
item.description: The Israeli army prevented a Palestinian American man from entering his home in the occupied West Bank town of Turmus Ayya, north of Ramallah, on Thursday and fired tear gas in the area, the homeowner told Anadolu Agency. Naji Abu Awad, who lives in the US state of Texas, said he arrived in his hometown carrying an American flag and his luggage and went to his house, but Israeli troops stationed inside prevented him from entering. He said he asked the soldiers why they were in his home and how long they intended to remain there, but was told the area had been designated a military zone and that he was not allowed to stay there. item.title: Trump says US ‘doesn’t need’ deal with Iran, claims control of Strait of Hormuz
item.description: President Donald Trump said Thursday that Washington no longer needs an agreement with Iran, claiming the US holds significant leverage over Tehran, including control of the Strait of Hormuz, Anadolu reports. “We don’t need a deal with Iran. Those days have long since passed,” Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform. He claimed that Washington secured Iranian financial assets and control of the strategically important waterway. “We’ve got their money, Hundreds of Billions of Dollars, and we’ve got their Strait!” he declared. The Strait of Hormuz, a vital global energy shipping route, has long been a flashpoint between Iran and the US, with tensions in the waterway carrying significant importance for international oil markets and regional security.
